gaps: FAA Part 107 knowledge test (UAG) fee: The official PSI/Talogy scheduling portal (faa.psiexams.com) confirms scheduling is available but does NOT publish the dollar fee amount on the pages retrieved; FAA pages state 'the test has a fee associated with it' without specifying the amount [18]. Fee must be confirmed directly with PSI/Talogy at time of scheduling.

FAA Remote Pilot Certificate processing time (temporary certificate): FAA states it 'anticipates issuing temporary certificates within 10 business days after receiving a completed application' [21], but this is a target, not a guarantee; permanent certificate takes 6–10 weeks per FAQ [31]. Combined range used (10 business days temp + up to 70 calendar days for permanent).

Texas Sales and Use Tax Permit applicability to commercial drone services: Whether specific drone services (photography, inspection, agricultural spraying) constitute 'taxable services' under Texas Tax Code is not confirmed by the official sources retrieved; a tax professional or Comptroller determination letter is needed [13][24].

TDA Commercial Applicator Business Registration (PAB-300) fee: The official TDA pages and PA-401 instructions reference the PAB-300 form but do NOT state its registration fee. Must be confirmed with TDA directly.

TDA Commercial Pesticide Applicator License processing time: No official TDA page states a standard processing time for license issuance; the application must be completed within one year [20], but turnaround after submission is not published.

FAA Part 137 Agricultural Aircraft Operator Certificate (AAOC) and exemption requirements: Drone operators applying pesticides by drone also need an FAA exemption from §107.36 and Part 137 regulations, plus an AAOC [8]. The exemption petition must be filed at least 120 days before intended operations. No fee is stated for the exemption or AAOC on the official pages retrieved.

Texas state-level insurance mandate for non-pesticide commercial drone operators: No Texas statute or regulatory page reviewed imposes a general liability insurance requirement on commercial drone businesses outside the pesticide context. Insurance is referenced by TDA for pesticide applicators only [10][19]; no equivalent state mandate confirmed for other commercial drone uses.

Local municipal permits (cities within Texas beyond Williamson County, e.g., Austin, Dallas, Houston, Plano): No city-level drone permit or fee schedule was confirmed from official municipal sources in the evidence set. Operators must check with each municipality where they intend to fly.

Remote ID Broadcast Module cost: The hardware cost of a compliant Remote ID broadcast module (if the drone is not a Standard Remote ID drone) is a market cost, not a government fee; no official fee schedule exists for this item.

FAA Part 107 waiver fees: The FAA waiver application (now via AIS Services) has no stated government fee on the pages reviewed [4]; processing time is 'up to 90 days' but is variable and not guaranteed.

Texas assumed name (DBA) certificate fee: If operating under a trade name, a DBA certificate must be filed with the county clerk in each county of operation [14]; county filing fees vary by county and were not confirmed in the evidence set.

Federal EIN (IRS): Required for business tax purposes; obtained free from IRS. Not confirmed as a Texas-specific requirement in evidence but universally required for business entities; IRS fee = $0 (online), not addressed in Texas official sources reviewed.
